exam_title: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

questions.question_text: Caustic soda is
questions.explanation: Caustic soda is the common chemical name for sodium hydroxide ($NaOH$).

questions.question_text: Which among the following preparation is used as a source of iodine in iodine deficiency ?
questions.explanation: Weak iodine solution (USP) contains 2% iodine and is traditionally used for iodine supplementation and antisepsis.

questions.question_text: In the assay of boric acid, glycerin is added to boric acid to
questions.explanation: Glycerin forms a complex with boric acid which behaves as a stronger monobasic acid, allowing it to be titrated accurately with sodium hydroxide.

questions.question_text: In cyanide poisoning, sodium nitrite is used as an antidote along with which compound ?
questions.explanation: Sodium nitrite induces methemoglobinemia to bind cyanide, and sodium thiosulfate converts cyanide to harmless thiocyanate via rhodanese.

questions.question_text: An antiseptic solution generally used for cleaning wounds and ears is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide releases oxygen and is widely used for mild wound cleaning and earwax removal.

questions.question_text: Drugs which help in eliminating exudations from bronchi are known as
questions.explanation: Expectorants assist in the expulsion of mucus and bronchial exudations.

questions.question_text: Calcium gluconate is assayed by
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate contains calcium ions which are typically quantified using EDTA complexometric titration.

questions.question_text: Chlorinated lime and boric acid solution is known as
questions.explanation: Eusol stands for Edinburgh University Solution of Antiseptic, which contains chlorinated lime and boric acid.

questions.question_text: Bleaching powder is
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is primarily composed of calcium oxychloride, commonly referred to as chlorinated lime.

questions.question_text: Nutritional deficiency of calcium leads to
questions.explanation: Deficiency of calcium in nutrition causes hypocalcemia.

questions.question_text: In radiation sterilization, the gamma rays were obtained from
questions.explanation: Cobalt-60 is the standard radioisotope used for gamma irradiation sterilization.

questions.question_text: Which among the following method is used for the sterilization of surgical dressings ?
questions.explanation: Surgical dressings and fabrics are effectively sterilized using steam under pressure (moist heat sterilization/autoclaving).

questions.question_text: Which among the following method represent the chemical cold sterilization method ?
questions.explanation: Gaseous agents such as ethylene oxide provide chemical cold sterilization without heat.

questions.question_text: The membrane filters used for sterilization has the pore size of
questions.explanation: Standard membrane filters for pharmaceutical sterilization typically have a pore size of $0.22 \mu m$.

questions.question_text: The optimum moisture content of the capsule shell is ranged between
questions.explanation: Hard gelatin capsule shells typically maintain an optimum moisture content of 12% to 15% to prevent brittleness or softening.

questions.question_text: The unequal distribution of colour on the surface of the tablet is known as
questions.explanation: Mottling is a tablet coating defect characterized by unequal color distribution.

questions.question_text: Which among the following material is used for enteric coating of tablet ?
questions.explanation: Cellulose acetate phthalate (CAP) is a classic pH-sensitive polymer used for enteric coating.

questions.question_text: The flow properties of the granules from hopper to die of the tablet machine is improved by the addition of
questions.explanation: Glidants are added to formulations to improve the flow characteristics of granules or powders.

questions.question_text: Which among the following capsule number represent the maximum capacity of the capsule ?
questions.explanation: Capsule size 000 is the largest standard hard gelatin capsule size, hence holding the maximum capacity.

questions.question_text: The plasticizer used in capsule shell is
questions.explanation: Glycerol (or glycerin) is commonly used as a plasticizer for gelatin shells to impart flexibility.

questions.question_text: Cupraloin test is used for the identification of
questions.explanation: The Cupraloin test specifically distinguishes isobarbaloin from other constituents in aloes.

questions.question_text: Give an example of Antidiabetic drug.
questions.explanation: Pterocarpus marsupium (malabar kino) is well known in traditional and herbal medicine for its antidiabetic properties.

questions.question_text: Reagent used in Ergotoxine test

options.A: Paramethyl amino benzaldehyde, sulphuric acid and ferric chloride
options.B: Amino ethyl benzaldehyde, sulphuric acid and ferric chloride
options.C: Paradimethyl amino benzaldehyde, sulphuric acid and ferric chloride
options.D: Diethyl amino benzaldehyde, sulphuric acid and ferric chloride

questions.explanation: Van Urk's reagent, containing p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde, sulfuric acid, and traces of ferric chloride, is used for ergot alkaloid testing.

questions.question_text: Rhubarb belongs to the family
questions.explanation: Rhubarb belongs to the family Polygonaceae.

questions.question_text: Steroid found in the flowers and leaves of Digitalis purpurea
questions.explanation: Digitalis purpurea contains cardiac glycosides like digitoxin and gitoxin containing genins such as digitoxigenin and gitoxigenin, whereas digoxigenin is characteristic of Digitalis lanata.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the substitute of cinchona bark ?
questions.explanation: Cuprea bark (Remijia cuprea) is a well-known commercial substitute for Cinchona bark.

questions.question_text: Senna consists of the

options.A: Dried leaflets of Cassia auriculata belongs to the family Liliaceae
options.B: Dried leaflets of Cassia acutifolia belongs to the family Leguminosae
options.C: Dried leaflets of Cassia fistula belongs to the family Liliaceae
options.D: Dried leaflets of Cassia auriculata belongs to the family Leguminosae

questions.explanation: Senna consists of dried leaflets of Cassia acutifolia (and Cassia angustifolia) belonging to the family Leguminosae.

questions.question_text: Gum resin derived from incision given on the stem of Commophora mukul is
questions.explanation: Guggul is the oleo-gum resin obtained from the stem of Commiphora mukul.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the purest form of Asafoetida ? i) Paste ii) Mass iii) Tear

options.D: All of the above i, ii and iii

questions.explanation: Tear and mass are recognized as natural forms of asafoetida, with tears being the purest resin form collected directly.

questions.question_text: Raw opium that has been treated to render it for smoking and that contains about eight percent of morphine is known as
questions.explanation: Prepared opium is raw opium processed and prepared for smoking purposes.

questions.question_text: Surfactants having HLB values between seven and nine ($7 - 9$) are
questions.explanation: Surfactants with an HLB value of 7 to 9 typically function as wetting and spreading agents.

questions.question_text: Water attack test is used for the detection of
questions.explanation: The water attack test is specifically designed to evaluate the chemical resistance of treated soda-lime glass (Type II glass).

questions.question_text: Give an example of indiffusible solid.
questions.explanation: Light kaolin is insoluble and does not readily mix or diffuse in water, making it an indiffusible solid.

questions.question_text: Green colour cap coding is used for packing of ophthalmic products containing
questions.explanation: Ophthalmic products containing steroids typically use a green color cap for identification according to standard regulatory conventions.

questions.question_text: Give an example of Cryoprotectants used in Parenterals.
questions.explanation: Polyethylene glycol and various sugars/polyols like mannitol are common cryoprotectants used to protect parenterals during freeze-drying.

questions.question_text: The sediment consists of loosely packed particles possessing a scaffolding like structure is seen in
questions.explanation: Flocculated suspensions form a loose, network-like (scaffolding) structure of sediment that is easy to redisperse.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used as an antiperspirant ?
questions.explanation: Aluminium chlorohydrate is a widely used active ingredient in antiperspirants to reduce sweating.

questions.question_text: Example for a cationic emulsifying agent
questions.explanation: Cetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide (CTAB) is a well-known quaternary ammonium cationic surfactant.

questions.question_text: Intravenous administration of calories, nitrogen and other nutrients in sufficient quantities to achieve tissue synthesis is called
questions.explanation: Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) refers to the intravenous provision of all essential nutrients required for tissue growth and maintenance.

questions.question_text: Depilatories are used as
questions.explanation: Depilatories are cosmetic preparations used to remove unwanted body hair.

questions.question_text: The stabilising agent used in making formaldehyde solution
questions.explanation: Methanol (typically 10-15%) is added to formalin to prevent the polymerization and precipitation of formaldehyde.

questions.question_text: Which chemical is given in conjugation with Isoniazid to avoid its neurotoxicity ?
questions.explanation: Pyridoxine (Vitamin $B_6$) is co-administered with isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy caused by pyridoxine depletion.

questions.question_text: Which therapeutic inactive compound is formed when beta lactamase hydrolyses the beta lactum ring ?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of the beta-lactam ring by beta-lactamases yields microbiologically inactive penicilloic acid derivatives (often grouped generally with penicillic/penicilloic degradation products).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a polyene antifungal antibiotic ?
questions.explanation: Amphotericin B is a classic polyene macrolide antifungal antibiotic.

questions.question_text: Fully substituted pyrimidine nucleus is found in
questions.explanation: Pyrimethamine contains a 2,4-diaminopyrimidine ring, representing a substituted pyrimidine nucleus.

questions.question_text: Which butyrophenone compound with therapeutic actions and uses are similar to phenothiazine ?
questions.explanation: Haloperidol is a potent butyrophenone antipsychotic with actions and uses similar to phenothiazines.

questions.question_text: Which form of adrenaline is having maximum biological activity ?
questions.explanation: The naturally occurring levo-isomer (L-adrenaline) possesses significantly higher biological activity than the dextro-isomer.

questions.question_text: Which salt of hyoscine is most stable and popularly accepted ?
questions.explanation: Hyoscine hydrobromide is the most commonly used and stable salt form of hyoscine (scopolamine).

questions.question_text: The substitute position of chlorine in chlorthiazide diuretic is
questions.explanation: In chlorothiazide, the chlorine substituent is situated at position 6 of the benzothiadiazine ring system.

questions.question_text: The antineoplastic drug containing pyrimidine nucleus
questions.explanation: Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a pyrimidine analog antineoplastic agent containing a fluorinated pyrimidine nucleus.

questions.question_text: Paracetamol overdosage is treated with
questions.explanation: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is the specific antidote used to treat paracetamol (acetaminophen) toxicity by replenishing glutathione stores.

questions.question_text: Inhibition of GABA transaminase enzyme is mainly done by
questions.explanation: Sodium valproate increases brain GABA levels partly by inhibiting GABA transaminase and succinic aldehyde dehydrogenase.

questions.question_text: The antiviral agent also used in treatment of Parkinsonism
questions.explanation: Amantadine is an antiviral medication that also has dopaminergic properties, making it useful in Parkinson's disease treatment.

questions.question_text: Diagnostic agent used in Myasthenia gravis
questions.explanation: Edrophonium is a short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used in the Tensilon test to diagnose Myasthenia gravis.

questions.question_text: The most potent mydriatic agent with longest duration of action
questions.explanation: Atropine is the most potent anticholinergic mydriatic with the longest duration of action (up to a week or more).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a second generation Antihistamine ?
questions.explanation: Promethazine is a first-generation antihistamine with pronounced sedative properties, unlike the non-sedating second-generation agents.

questions.question_text: The cardiac glycoside commonly given by parenteral route in emergency
questions.explanation: Ouabain (strophanthin-G) has a rapid onset and was historically used parenterally in acute cardiac emergencies.

questions.question_text: The angiotensin receptor antagonist used in hypertension
questions.explanation: Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB), whereas captopril and enalapril are ACE inhibitors.

questions.question_text: Insulin is usually given to diabetic patients by which route ?
questions.explanation: Insulin is a peptide hormone that is degraded in the gastrointestinal tract, so it is typically administered via the subcutaneous route.

questions.question_text: The drug of choice for treatment of Typhoid fever is
questions.explanation: Historically and classically, chloramphenicol has been recognized as the quintessential drug of choice for treating typhoid fever.

questions.question_text: The licence for wholesale of drugs specified in Schedule X is issued in
questions.explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, Form 20G is used for issuing a license to sell, stock, or exhibit for sale by wholesale drugs specified in Schedule X.

questions.question_text: Anyone who contravenes any provision of the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act shall on first conviction be liable to

options.A: 1 month of imprisonment or fine or both
options.B: 3 months of imprisonment or fine or both
options.C: 6 months of imprisonment or fine or both
options.D: 1 year of imprisonment or fine or both

questions.explanation: First conviction under the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act carries imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both.

questions.question_text: Offences committed under NDPS Act, 1985 shall be triable by the Special Court constituted under the Act, where the punishment is
questions.explanation: Under the NDPS Act, offences carrying a punishment of imprisonment for more than 3 years are triable by a Special Court.

questions.question_text: Intra-uterine devices are tested at
questions.explanation: Intra-uterine devices (IUDs) and condoms are tested for quality at the Indian Pharmacopoeial Laboratory (IPL) in Ghaziabad.

questions.question_text: Loan licence is issued under Drugs and Cosmetics Act for the manufacture of drugs other than those specified in
questions.explanation: Loan licenses cannot be issued for drugs specified in Schedule X due to their strict psychotropic and narcotic control requirements.

questions.question_text: Drug inspectors should intimate the purpose of taking drug samples to the person concerned in
questions.explanation: Form 17 is the formal document used by Drug Inspectors to disclose the purpose and receipt of taking drug samples for analysis.

questions.question_text: The first Central Council was constituted by the Central Government in
questions.explanation: The first Pharmacy Council of India (Central Council) was constituted in the year 1949 under the Pharmacy Act, 1948.

questions.question_text: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Order came into force in
questions.explanation: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Control, Regulation and Review Order came into force in 1993.

questions.question_text: If a drug contains any harmful or toxic substance, which may render it injurious to health, it is called
questions.explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, a drug containing any filthy, putrid, or decomposed substance, or any harmful/toxic ingredient rendering it injurious to health, is deemed an adulterated drug.

questions.question_text: The number of nominated members to the State Pharmacy Council are
questions.explanation: State Pharmacy Councils consist of 6 members nominated by the State Government under Section 19 of the Pharmacy Act.

questions.question_text: Inventories moving temporarily because of seasonal production are called
questions.explanation: Surplus or seasonal inventory refers to items that accumulate temporarily due to seasonal production fluctuations.

questions.question_text: A modern drug store should fulfil all minimum requirements as specified in ___________ of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules 1945.
questions.explanation: Schedule N outlines the minimum requirements for the efficient running of a pharmacy or modern drug store.

questions.question_text: One among the following is not a source of secondary data for market research
questions.explanation: Sales turnover represents primary internal company data rather than external or published secondary data.

questions.question_text: The method in which a code is assigned to stored items for easy identification is called
questions.explanation: Mnemonic coding uses letters and abbreviations to help easily remember and identify stored items.

questions.question_text: The inventory carrying cost is represented by items like (i) Cost of insurance (ii) Cost of paper work (iii) Cost of taxes (iv) Cost of posting
questions.explanation: Cost of insurance and taxes are direct holding/carrying costs associated with storing inventory.

questions.question_text: The capital necessary to maintain a minimum level of stock and for payment of regular expenses is called
questions.explanation: Permanent working capital represents the minimum amount of liquid capital required continuously to maintain essential stock and operations.

questions.question_text: The bank launched in India for promoting the export and import of goods and services is
questions.explanation: The Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank) was established for promoting international trade and financing exports/imports.

questions.question_text: The lower limit below which the stock of any item, should not normally be allowed to fall is
questions.explanation: Buffer stock (or safety stock) is the minimum reserve level maintained to prevent stockouts.

questions.question_text: The items which consume 70% of the total budget of inventories, but represent only 10% of the total inventory are called
questions.explanation: In ABC analysis, 'A' items account for the highest value consumption (~70%) despite making up a small percentage (~10%) of total items.

questions.question_text: Pre-determined scrap is refered to as
questions.explanation: Anticipated or planned scrap is estimated in advance before manufacturing or processing begins.

questions.question_text: The efficiency of HEPA filter can be tested using
questions.explanation: The DOP (dioctyl phthalate) smoke test is a standard method used to test the integrity and efficiency of HEPA filters.

questions.question_text: Pharmacy and Therapeutic Committee has role except in

options.B: Preparation of drug list and emergency supplies

questions.explanation: Medical record services are managed by the health information management department, not the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) committee.

questions.question_text: MEDLINE is a drug information resource categorised under
questions.explanation: MEDLINE is a bibliographic database indexing biomedical literature, making it a secondary literature resource.

questions.question_text: Test for water holding capacity is stated in Indian Pharmacopoeia for
questions.explanation: Absorbent cotton wool is tested for its water holding capacity according to pharmacopoeial standards.

questions.question_text: ‘Clean room area’ means

options.A: Socially clean area free from particulate matter
options.D: Area with high standards of cleanliness and hygiene

questions.explanation: A clean room is defined as a socially clean area controlled for airborne particulate matter and environmental parameters.

questions.question_text: Satellite pharmacy a mode of drug distribution system under
questions.explanation: Satellite pharmacies operate as decentralized units to dispense medications close to nursing units, typically in decentralized unit dose systems.

questions.question_text: Automatic stop order is used for
questions.explanation: Automatic stop orders are policies applied to dangerous or controlled drugs (such as narcotics and sedatives) to limit prolonged unmonitored use.

questions.question_text: Absorbable suture is
questions.explanation: Chromic catgut is a natural absorbable surgical suture, unlike nylon, silk, and cotton which are non-absorbable.

questions.question_text: Tuberculin syringe is available in
questions.explanation: Tuberculin syringes are small-volume syringes typically designed with a capacity of 1 ml for accurate intradermal administration.

questions.question_text: Which one is used for aspiration of stomach contents ?
questions.explanation: Ryle's tube (nasogastric tube) is inserted through the nose into the stomach for feeding or aspiration of gastric contents.

questions.question_text: Withdrawal symptoms of opioids can be managed with
questions.explanation: Methadone is a long-acting mu-opioid receptor agonist used for detoxification and maintenance therapy in opioid dependence.

questions.question_text: Bioavailability increases when drugs are in
questions.explanation: Non-ionized drugs are lipophilic and can easily cross biological lipid membranes, thus increasing absorption and bioavailability.

questions.question_text: Insulin induced hypoglycaemia is classified under
questions.explanation: Type A ADRs are dose-dependent, predictable extensions of a drug's pharmacological action, such as hypoglycemia caused by insulin.

questions.question_text: A method to improve patient compliance is
questions.explanation: All listed methods (counselling, proper labeling, and regimen simplification) effectively enhance patient medication adherence.

questions.question_text: Serum sodium level is
questions.explanation: The normal physiological reference range for serum sodium in humans is approximately 135 to 145 mmol/L.

questions.question_text: Metoclopramide if given with paracetamol
questions.explanation: Metoclopramide accelerates gastric emptying, thereby increasing the rate of absorption and decreasing the onset time of analgesia for paracetamol.

questions.question_text: Fatigue, weight loss, chronic cough, night sweats, chest pain are clinical symptoms of
questions.explanation: Chronic cough, night sweats, fatigue, and weight loss are classic hallmark symptoms of pulmonary tuberculosis.

questions.question_text: HBsAg testing is done to detect the presence of
questions.explanation: HBsAg (Hepatitis B surface antigen) is a serological marker specifically used to screen for Hepatitis B virus infection.

questions.question_text: Amphetamine poisoning can be treated with
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate alkalinizes the urine, which ionizes amphetamines and enhances their renal excretion during overdose.

questions.question_text: If two or more dosage forms of same drug contain same labelled quantities of the drug, they are
questions.explanation: Products that contain the same active ingredients in the exact same labeled quantities are defined as chemical equivalents.
